description:
North-star capstone for OUTRAM PARK: drive an end-to-end reactor multiphysics
simulation FROM a Final Safety Analysis Report (FSAR)-level plant description,
including radiological source-term calculations.

Vision: given an FSAR-level input (geometry, materials, core loading, operating
envelope, design-basis accident/transient scenarios), produce:
  1. Nuclear data + multigroup cross sections (njoy-outram-park-fork).
  2. Geometry/mesh + Monte Carlo reference (outram-mc-libs / OpenMC-like).
  3. Coupled multiphysics: deterministic neutronics (GeN-Foam diffusion/SP3/SN) +
     thermal-hydraulics + thermo-mechanics + point kinetics (teh-o-prke), over the
     transient/accident scenarios.
  4. Source-term calculations: fission-product inventory + depletion/transmutation
     (outram-mc-libs depletion), release fractions + transport (boon-lay /
     TRISO-ATOPS Eulerian + Lagrangian), coolant activity / plate-out, and the
     released radionuclide source term.
  5. V&V against published FSAR / benchmark transients.

Ties together essentially the whole suite (njoy -> openmc -> genfoam -> source
terms), with nee_soon as the coupling/orchestration layer and, later, KOVAN to
extract FSAR/thesis inputs into structured form. Long-term / aspirational --
matures as each pillar matures; depends on op-cjw (nuclear data), op-u6s (MC),
op-p6p (GeN-Foam multiphysics), op-b4a (source terms/TRISO release), op-fr2
(nee_soon coupling).

INTENDED-USE (mandatory, RESPONSIBLE_USE.md): OUTRAM PARK is for education,
research, capability-building, and V&V ONLY. This epic is NOT for real FSAR
preparation, licensing, safety-critical decision-making, or operational/emergency
use, and must not be framed as authoritative for any of those.
title: FSAR-to-multiphysics simulation with source-term calculations (capstone vision)

acceptance_criteria: Written feasibility assessment committed (FV-vs-FEM mapping, GeN-Foam overlap, recommended path + effort estimate); no large implementation until the recommendation is accepted.
description: Investigate translating Moltres (MOOSE-based, MSRE-VALIDATED MSR multiphysics: group neutron diffusion + drift-flux delayed-neutron precursors + salt TH) into an OpenFOAM-style finite-volume formulation on outram-foam, rather than porting MOOSE (which is finite-element + PETSc + MPI and is banned by the workspace no-FFI/no-PETSc/no-MPI rule). FEASIBILITY IS UNCERTAIN and this bead is a SPIKE first, not a commitment. Key finding to weigh in design: GeN-Foam (GPL-3, already the on-hold OpenFOAM port parked in outram-foam-appbuilder-lib) ALREADY implements circulating-fuel neutronics + delayed-neutron precursor drift + TH in a finite-volume OpenFOAM setting — so reviving/extending the GeN-Foam port may be the better vehicle, with Moltres used as the reference formulation + validation yardstick (it is validated against MSRE). Deliverable of this bead: a written feasibility assessment (FV vs FEM mapping of the drift-flux precursor + group-diffusion equations; overlap with GeN-Foam; recommended path) BEFORE any large implementation. LICENSE: Moltres LGPL/GPL — reference use; verify before reusing any code. Untrusted AI-assisted draft pending human V&V.
design: Spike: map Moltres's group-diffusion + circulating-precursor + salt-TH equation set onto outram-foam FV operators; compare against GeN-Foam's existing circulating-fuel implementation; recommend (a) extend GeN-Foam port vs (b) fresh Moltres-formulation port. Output = assessment doc + recommendation, not production code.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: License due-diligence (2026-08-04): Moltres = arfc/moltres (UIUC ARFC), LGPL -> GPLv3-COMPATIBLE (LGPL code may be used in a GPL-3 work). OK as reference AND for code reuse if desired. Confirmed MOOSE-based finite-element (PETSc) -> a direct MOOSE port is banned (no-FFI/PETSc/MPI rule); this bead stays a feasibility spike mapping Moltres's validated MSR formulation onto outram-foam FV / the existing GeN-Foam port.

title: Feasibility + spike: translate Moltres physics into an OpenFOAM (outram-foam) formulation, not MOOSE

description: One of the picked items + a roadmap MC-coupling child. Extend to_mc_geometry beyond fitted primitives/convex: emit the faceted-solid route (a general CsgSurface::Plane per triangle, DAGMC-style) so ANY closed mesh exports to outram-mc-libs CSG, feeding the Monte Carlo neutronics side of the coupled sims. Currently returns ExportError::NotImplemented for a general plane. Depends on mc-export feature (present). V&V: a non-convex L-prism exports to an MC Geometry whose inside-test matches the mesh (interior point inside, notch point outside).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: BLOCKED on outram-mc-libs (2026-07-24 finding): SurfaceKind has only XPlane/YPlane/ZPlane/Sphere/ZCylinder — NO general Plane{a,b,c,d}, no faceted/mesh volume. to_mc_geometry therefore cannot emit a general (non-axis-aligned) plane; even a ROTATED CONVEX mesh is blocked, not just non-convex. Blender side is already ready: export::to_csg_primitive emits general CsgSurface::Plane for the convex-faceted path, and export::to_faceted_solid gives the DAGMC-style non-convex boundary (triangles + winding inside-test). PREREQUISITE (in outram-mc-libs, owned by the outram-mc session): (1) add SurfaceKind::Plane{a,b,c,d} (evaluate=a*x+b*y+c*z-d, ray distance, half-space sense) -> unlocks convex-faceted meshes; (2) a faceted-volume / DAGMC surface-tracking cell for TRUE non-convex. Do NOT edit outram-mc-libs from the blender branch without coordination (merge-conflict risk with the parallel outram-mc session). Awaiting maintainer decision on ownership.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: PARTIAL (commit a942f81): the CONVEX-faceted MC export path is now UNBLOCKED — outram-mc-libs has a general Plane{a,b,c,d} surface (the old NotImplemented gate was stale), so to_mc_geometry now maps CsgSurface::Plane -> SurfaceKind::Plane and any convex polyhedron exports (one half-space/face). STILL OPEN for this bead: genuinely NON-convex meshes (faceted-solid/DAGMC) still need a real outram-mc-libs faceted-solid dependency; to_faceted_solid produces only the local mirror. So op-hzs.36 (non-convex) remains, but convex-faceted is done.

title: outram-blender: mc-export for non-convex meshes (faceted-solid/DAGMC -> outram-mc CSG)
